title: Sardinian Restaurants Ask Families to Put Phones Away
paragraphs: Going out for a meal with your family should be a chance to enjoy good food and spend time together. But these days, it's common to see everyone looking at their phones or watching videos on tablets instead of talking.
Now, some restaurants on the Italian island of Sardinia are trying to change that.

Starting in early November, 15 restaurants are encouraging parents and children to put away their phones and other electronic devices during meals, so they can spend more time talking and enjoying their meals together.
The project, called "At the Table Without Screens," will run for one month at first, and more restaurants may join later.
Families visiting these restaurants can choose whether to take part in the project. Those who agree are asked to leave their devices in their bags or put them in a basket at the table.
But the restaurants aren't just asking families to stop using their phones — they're also giving them something else to do.

Families receive a special kit with games, drawing activities and other things to help parents and children talk more. They can play games while waiting for their food, or use the activities as a starting point for conversations.
The kit also includes advice for parents on children's screen time and social media use at home.
The project is led by Anna Cau, Sardinia's children's ombudsman. She believes parents need more support to help their children use technology safely.
Emanuele Frongia, the head of a restaurant association in Sardinia, says dining out should be a time for families to talk and enjoy each other's company.
"But adults must set a good example first," he said. "We can't ask children to put away their phones if we're not willing to do the same."
